text:
incident-bot: SEV: HIGH — surge detected: fncall invocations x3.8, structured-output validation failures rising, 5xx up and GPU queue latched on rt-pool-7. Auto-page to oncall. Dash: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/surge-summary

maya: Ack. I'm live. Seeing a tight cohort of tenants replaying long tool chains. Many of those chains emit large JSONs that trigger retries. Starting triage.

felix: Correlation: a change in route-optimizer merged smaller batches into big batched fncalls — increased memory pressure and KV cache thrash. Pod restarts starting ~13:08 UTC.

ops-chef: We should opt for a minimal-impact mitigation first: gate fncalls at the edge per-tier for 15m. We have the edge toggle rtrctl set feature fncall-gate.<@maya> can you flip for non-enterprise?

maya: Executing safe toggle: ```rtrctl set feature fncall-gate --scope=non-enterprise --state=hold --reason="surge-1765439999"``` Got 200. Applying to free/early-adopter/partner_trial.

incident-bot: FNCall gate applied for: free, early-adopter, partner_trial. Monitoring 60s.

sam: Meanwhile, structured-output is still heavy. We can reduce payloads by switching structured_output.profile to "compact" which strips verbose annotations and size-heavy fields. There's a runtime flag: RO_STRUCTURED_PROFILE.

maya: Patching config: ```curl -s -X PATCH https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/configs -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" -d '{"RO_STRUCTURED_PROFILE":"compact","scope":"non-enterprise"}'``` Returned 202. Rolling on us-west1/us-east1.

support-lead: Heads-up — apps depending on full JSON may error; support queue will spike. I'm drafting a short notice and FAQ.

felix: I'm scaling down the route-optimizer rollout to stop aggressive merge. Command: ```kubectl -n runtime scale deploy/route-optimizer --replicas=1``` Also adding a quick guard to prevent >8 concurrency per batch. Patching configmap route-optimizer.conf concurrency_limit=8.

maya: Early effects: fncall QPS down ~65% from gated tiers, GPU queue depth normalized on rt-pool-7, p95 latency -22%. p99 still elevated, seeing some noisy tenants retrying.

ops-chef: For repeat offenders let's limit tenant burst tokens. Implement temporary per-tenant token bucket: 15 fncalls/min, 128KB structured payload/min for 30m. Use rl-api.

sam: rl-api calls: ```POST /rl/v1/update -d '{"scope":"tenant","metric":"fncall","limit":"15/m","ttl":"30m"}'``` and ```POST /rl/v1/update -d '{"metric":"structured_size","limit":"131072/m","ttl":"30m"}'```. Applying now.

incident-bot: Rate-limits active. Alert thresholds tuned to new limits.

support-lead: Please export list of tenants that hit the new caps so we can contact them directly. Prefer CSV.

maya: Querying telemetry: ```psql -h telemetry -c "COPY (SELECT tenant_id, count(*) FROM fncall_hits WHERE ts > now() - interval '20 minutes' GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 200) TO STDOUT WITH CSV" > /tmp/tenants-surge.csv"``` Sending to support secure channel.

felix: Also toggled fallback model on degrades to redwood-lite for tool-rendered content to reduce GPU footprint: ```controlplane set model-fallback --threshold=0.05 --fallback=redwood-lite```. This affects streaming that still allows small fncalls.

maya: Summary of actions: 1) edge fncall gate on non-enterprise 2) structured_output.profile=compact for non-enterprise 3) rollback/scale-down of route-optimizer batching 4) per-tenant burst caps 5) model fallback to redwood-lite 6) monitoring and tenant list export

sam: Next: keep mitigations 30m, then staged re-enable: allow limited fncalls with backoff + stricter retry headers. Also add defensive validation to structured-output path to drop excessive nested arrays earlier.

support-lead: Sending short customer note now: "We're applying temporary limits to automated tool calls and structured JSON outputs for lower tiers to restore service stability. Enterprise tenants unaffected. We're emailing affected customers with details and timeline."

incident-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-0479 created, severity S3, page handoff to night oncall.

maya: Handing to @oncall-night for watch. If p99 climbs again, escalate to me and we'll consider tenant quarantine (hard block) for repeat offenders.

oncall-night: Ack, taking watch. I'll check dashboards every 5m and watch the cap list. If any tenant hits >3 breaches, propose quarantine and a rollback of structured compact to text-only if needed.

felix: 13:40 UTC status: p95 within normal, p99 down ~18% from peak. No new 5xx spikes. Keeping caps until 14:10 UTC.

support-lead: Preparing postmortem stub and will capture mitigation timeline and exact commands. Tagging SRE rotation for follow-up.

incident-bot: This thread will remain open. Add updates or use `/incident update INC-2026-0479` to append timeline. :white_check_mark:
